subject: Mutual action plan: capacity runway, GPU pool sizing & lead-time windows
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Dana Park <dana.park@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action plan kickoff: capacity runway, GPU pool sizing & lead-time windows

Dana —

Thanks again for the call today. As discussed, I’m starting a short MAP thread to lock down the capacity reservation plan and the evaluation-to-commit timeline for EdgeHealth’s Private deployment. Key asks from your side were: target go-live window (Q4), regulatory acceptance testing (SOC2 evidence), and an initial GPU pool that supports your 5k concurrent inference QPS target for images.

Attached is an initial sizing workbook with three scenarios (Conservative / Base / Aggressive) and an early-leadtime matrix that reflects Dedicated and Private procurement paths. Highlights:
- Base scenario: 24 x A100-equivalent GPUs (quantized serving) — implies ~8–12 week lead time for Dedicated reserved pools in our standard regions.
- Aggressive: 40 x A100-equivalent — requires tranche ordering and possible special procurement; ~14–18 week lead time.
- Fallbacks: we can route traffic to hosted instances for first 6–8 weeks if device delivery slips; we recommend enabling prefix caching and continuous batching to reduce peak requirements during ramp.

Can you confirm the target contract signature date range (you mentioned mid-August as possible) and whether EdgeHealth needs on-prem provisioning (air-gapped) or VPC? That will materially change lead time and acceptance windows.

Proposed next steps (high level):
1) You confirm target sign date and deployment mode (VPC vs on-prem) by Tue 6/22.
2) Redwood provides a final MAP with milestone dates and acceptance gates by Fri 6/25.
3) Joint evaluation sprint (2 weeks) followed by staging handoff.

Attachments: edgehealth_gpu_sizing_scenarios_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks — looping Karthik in for sizing & Marissa for procurement cadence.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Dana Park <dana.park@edgehealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@edgehealth.com, Alex Li <alex.li@edgehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan kickoff: capacity runway, GPU pool sizing & lead-time windows

Sofia —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the workbook. A few clarifications from procurement and infra:
- Our preferred signature window is Aug 9–20, 2026 (we have an internal board review the week of Aug 2).
- We will be VPC (no air-gap) but need proof of SOC2 controls before signing. Can Redwood provide the SOC2 evidence package and a SOC2-scope checklist tied to the MAP?
- On sizing: our internal benchmarks were more conservative — we were expecting to start with ~16 A100-equivalents and then scale. Is that realistic if we optimize prompts and enable quantization?

Questions for Redwood:
1) If we agree on a 16 GPU starting pool, what does the acceptance timetable look like (staging -> production)?
2) If Dedicated procurement takes 12 weeks and our sign window is mid-August, when would we realistically hit production?

We’re fine with a short evaluation sprint. Procurement will need a clear list of deliverables linked to each milestone (SOC2 docs, data retention settings, and network diagram).

—
Dana Park
Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeHealth
dana.park@edgehealth.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Dana Park <dana.park@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 07:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan kickoff: capacity runway, GPU pool sizing & lead-time windows

Dana — thanks for the details and the August window — that helps a lot. Quick answers and a proposed milestone table below. I’ve also attached a short MAP PDF (redwood_map_timeline_v2.pdf) that maps deliverables to procurement gates.

Short answers to your questions:
1) 16 GPUs is doable as a starting pool if you take the following optimizations: prompt batching, 8-bit quantization profiles for non-critical models, and enabling prefix caching for common flows. With those settings we project ~70–80% of the Base throughput for the Base cost. I’ve put a scenario in the spreadsheet labelled “Base-Optimized (16)” with perf estimates.
2) Dedicated procurement timing: our standard slotting puts a ~10–12 week lead time once contract is fully executed for VPC-backed Dedicated pools in the us-west region. If you sign in the Aug 9–20 window, a reasonable production target would be late October / early November (assuming acceptance goes smoothly). If you need earlier availability, we can chain-hosted bursts behind the Dedicated pool for the first 6–8 weeks post-signature.

Proposed MAP milestones (summary):
- M1 (Sign): Contract signature (Target: Aug 9–20) — procurement checklist delivered to EdgeHealth.
- M2 (Eval Sprint): 2-week evaluation (Target: Aug 23–Sep 3) — deliverables: validation prompt set, latency/cost baseline, SOC2 evidence snapshot.
- M3 (Staging): Provision staging pool (2 weeks post-eval) — handoff acceptance checklist, security review.
- M4 (Production): Dedicated pool live (10–12 weeks post-sign) or earlier with hosted-burst fallback.

Action items:
- Dana / procurement: confirm sign window in writing by EOD Tue 6/22 so we can lock procurement slots.
- Marissa: I’ll hand off the procurement checklist and draft SOW to you for prep.
- Karthik: please confirm the sizing numbers in the Base-Optimized tab and call out any additional infra constraints (network egress, HSM/KMS).

Attachments: redwood_map_timeline_v2.pdf

Thanks — I’ll collate this into a formal MAP doc once we have confirmation.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dana Park <dana.park@edgehealth.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan kickoff: capacity runway, GPU pool sizing & lead-time windows

Dana / team —

Thanks for the clarity, Dana. If Aug 9–20 is the window, we’ll tentatively reserve procurement capacity for EdgeHealth this week to avoid a later tranche sell-through. Can you confirm by EOD today (22 June)? Once you confirm, I’ll circulate a short non-binding procurement reservation note (internal) and send a preliminary commercial term sheet + DocuSign link for a draft order (no signatures required to hold slot, but it helps our vendor team prioritize).

DocuSign (draft): https://app.docusign.com/link/EDGE-1492-draft-order

We’ll also attach the SOC2 evidence pack to the MAP draft that Sofia will share.

—
Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
